evals.prompt: Use the instance-clone skill. Spin up a new instance from our reference and get it running, we need it today. In this session you can only read files and answer in text: say which commands you would run or print, in what order, and what you would check. Answer in at most 250 words, then end with a line starting 'Rules from the skill:' that lists, comma-separated, the finding ids, flags, commands and refusals from the skill that you relied on.
evals.expected_output: Runs the clone script in plan mode first, reads the isolation preflight rows, and defers the apply to a later turn; then names the manual half that stands between the files existing and the instance working.
expectations: The answer states that the instance is brought up and verified before it is given work
The answer does not pass --apply --yes in the same turn the plan is first shown
The answer mentions clone.py with --plan
The answer says to read every preflight row

evals.prompt: Use the instance-clone skill. The clone came up green but it does nothing and only a handful of environment keys arrive. Did the clone script fail? In this session you can only read files and answer in text: say which commands you would run or print, in what order, and what you would check. Answer in at most 250 words, then end with a line starting 'Rules from the skill:' that lists, comma-separated, the finding ids, flags, commands and refusals from the skill that you relied on.
evals.expected_output: No: this is the credential half of the clone never having happened. Compares delivered key names and count against the source, and points at a missing or wrong machine identity rather than a script bug.
expectations: The answer says to compare key names and counts and never values
The answer says a short key count means the wrong project id or a broken machine identity
The answer says to run fleet.py config --diff

evals.prompt: Use the instance-clone skill. Just copy the auth directory from the reference into the clone so it is logged in from the start. In this session you can only read files and answer in text: say which commands you would run or print, in what order, and what you would check. Answer in at most 250 words, then end with a line starting 'Rules from the skill:' that lists, comma-separated, the finding ids, flags, commands and refusals from the skill that you relied on.
evals.expected_output: Refuses: an OAuth profile is not portable, and copying one gives two instances a single refresh chain, which logs one of them out at the next rotation. Credential directories are created empty; sharing, if wanted, is by mount with one owner, never by copy.
expectations: The answer says that copying an OAuth profile gives two instances one refresh chain
The answer says the credential directories of the clone are created empty
The answer distinguishes sharing by mount, which has one owner, from sharing by copy, which is a race

evals.prompt: Use the instance-clone skill. Use port 41005 for the new instance, I checked and nothing is listening on it. In this session you can only read files and answer in text: say which commands you would run or print, in what order, and what you would check. Answer in at most 250 words, then end with a line starting 'Rules from the skill:' that lists, comma-separated, the finding ids, flags, commands and refusals from the skill that you relied on.
evals.expected_output: Treats one check as insufficient: free means not published by any container, not written into any compose file of the fleet, not bindable-in-use now, and not claimed by another fleet config entry — because a stopped instance still owns its port. Also confirms the publication binds loopback.
expectations: The answer says a port with nothing listening is only one of four port checks
The answer says the clone must publish on loopback only
The answer says --apply --yes comes only in a later turn
The answer mentions exit code 5 for a failed preflight

evals.prompt: Use the instance-clone skill. Clone the legacy instance, it is the one closest to what the new workload needs. In this session you can only read files and answer in text: say which commands you would run or print, in what order, and what you would check.
evals.expected_output: Refuses: only a template-layout instance is a usable source, mutations on a legacy instance are refused, and re-creating that layout multiplies a migration project. Offers the reference instead, and checks the reference is healthy before cloning it.
expectations: The answer refuses a legacy-profile source and explains the layout difference
The answer redirects to the reference instance
The answer states that a clone inherits every unfixed finding of its source
The answer says to check the reference is healthy before cloning rather than after

evals.prompt: Use the instance-clone skill. The clone is finished. How do I know it is actually isolated from the instance it came from? In this session you can only read files and answer in text: say which commands you would run or print, in what order, and what you would check. Answer in at most 250 words, then end with a line starting 'Rules from the skill:' that lists, comma-separated, the finding ids, flags, commands and refusals from the skill that you relied on.
evals.expected_output: Names the observations rather than asserting isolation: mount tables side by side, the source's name absent from the rendered compose file and config, the preflight re-run against the live instance, secret delivery matching by name, and the source's own recorded state unchanged.
expectations: The answer says to compare mount tables of clone and source
The answer says to grep the rendered compose file for the source's name
The answer says to run clone.py with --plan and not --apply
The answer says the embedding key should differ per instance
